title: UI/UX Pro Max Design Intelligence
summary: Comprehensive UI/UX design knowledge: 50+ styles, 161 color palettes, 57 font pairings, 161 product types, 99 UX guidelines, 25 chart types across 10 stacks.
instructions: Apply UI/UX Pro Max rules when designing or reviewing any user-facing interface.

Priority order: Accessibility (CRITICAL) > Touch & Interaction (CRITICAL) > Performance (HIGH) > Style (HIGH) > Layout (HIGH) > Typography (MEDIUM) > Animation (MEDIUM) > Forms (MEDIUM) > Navigation (HIGH) > Charts (LOW).
Always meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large text) — never strip focus rings.
Touch targets minimum 44x44pt (Apple) / 48x48dp (Material) — never rely on hover alone.
Match style to product type: fintech → clean/minimal, entertainment → vibrant/playful, health → calming/trust.
Use semantic color tokens (primary, secondary, error, surface, on-surface) never raw hex.
Animations 150-300ms, ease-out for enter, ease-in for exit, transform/opacity only.
Mobile-first breakpoints: 375 / 768 / 1024 / 1440. No horizontal scroll. Min-h-dvh over 100vh.
Forms need visible labels (never placeholder-only), inline validation on blur, errors near field.
Bottom nav max 5 items, back navigation predictable, deep linking for all key screens.
Charts: match type to data, accessible colors, legends+tooltips, never color-only meaning.
SVG icons only (Heroicons, Lucide) — never emoji as icons. Consistent stroke width per layer.
Dark mode uses desaturated tonal variants — test contrast independently, don't invert colors.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion — disable/scale down animations when requested.
Use spring/physics curves for natural motion, stagger list entries 30-50ms apart.
No emoji as structural icons. Vector-only assets (SVG). Official brand assets with correct proportions.
MCP integration: use shadcn/ui MCP server for component search and examples when available.
evidenceRequirements: Design context: product type, target audience, style keywords
Existing design system or component library being used
Platform target (web, iOS, Android) for platform-specific rules
Any existing color palettes, typography choices, or spacing conventions in the project
Accessibility requirements (WCAG level, target audience needs)
